description.narrative: Det övergripande målet är att ungdomar och unga vuxna i östra och södra Afrika genom ökad egenmakt och motståndskraft, i ökad utsträckning engagerar sig, skapar nätverk och förbättrar sin sexuella och reproduktiva hälsa och rättigheter. Målet ska uppnås genom fyra övergripande outcomes; - Ökat regionalt ansvar för SRHR påskyndar medlemsländernas förverkligande av Agenda 2063 och SDG 3. - Attityder och handlingar bland rättighetsbärare, de som formar normer, och unga är i ökad grad stödjande av ungas SRHR - Unga tar en ökad roll i sin egen hälsa och i system för hälsa. - Förbättrad SRHR bland unga genom att komponenter av effektiva modeller för ungas SRHR genomförs.

The goal is to ensure that adolescents and young people in Eastern and Southern Africa with improved access to quality sexual and reproductive health and wellness services, enjoy increased health, agency, and resilience. This will be achieved through four main outcomes: - Increased regional accountability for SRHR accelerates member states' realisation of Agenda 2030 and SDG 3. - Growing support among targeted duty bearers, norms makers, and young people for adolescent sexual and reproductive health and rights (ASRHR), is reflected in their attitudes and actions. - Empowered and networked young people play an increased role in their own health and in systems for health. - Targeted implementation of effective ASRHR models in SADC members states improves adolescent health outcomes.

title.narrative: Grant agreement between Sida and Sexual Reproductive Health and Rights Africa Trust

description.narrative:
SAT had a delayed start of phase 2 due to Sida not being able to approve the budget and workplan until October 2023, which resulted in a limited implementation time of the previous reporting period. Nevertheless, some of the results that were achieved between July to December 2023 include:
Longterm result 1: Increased Regional Accountability for SRHR Accelerates Member States Realisation of Agenda 2063 And SDG 3. SAT focused on 3 regional accountability mechanisms to accelrate SRHR for termination of pregnancy and condom access: 1) the Addis Ababa Declaration on Population and Development, 2) the SADC PF Regional Standing Committees, and 3) the SADC SRHR Scorecard. For ex. SAT supported AfriYAN chapters in the region to conduct member state level youthled reviews of over 50 national laws, policies and strategies with a view for recommendations to be made to the continental review in Lusaka ahead of the Review of the Addis Ababa Declaration on Population and Development. In total, SAT supported participation of 548 representatives of civil society, including young people in the policy, delivery, & accountability spaces, places, and processes with regards to SRHR.
Longterm result 2: Growing support among targeted duty bearers, norms makers, and young people for adolescent sexual and reproductive health and rights (ASRHR), reflected in their attitudes and actions. In SAT's programme countries, SAT serves in 37 task forces or Technical Working Groups (TWGs). In 22 of these, SAT is represented by young people, who receive continuous support, capacity, and mentorship to enable them to engage fully in the structures and processes. In total, SAT supported young people to participate in 167 public events, which included technical working groups, workshops, national commemoration days, workshops, and other such public fora.
Longterm result 3: Empowered and networked young people play an increased role in their own health and in systems for health. Working through 6 youth hubs in SAT countries, SAT built the capacity of youth activists as well as established working partnerships with allies in the ASRHR space in order to advocate for improved ASRHR systems for health, thereby creating 15 such networks. SAT also strengthened the capacity of 241 youth hubsters to engage in ASRHR places and spaces.
Longterm result 4: Targeted implementation of effective ASRHR models in SADC member states improves adolescent health outcomes. A total of 8,105 young people registered on SAT's system YouthWize and reported on 4,384 cases in the communityled monitoring. 2 surveys with key population groups (AGYW and LGBTQI) were undertaken to understand issues around ASRHR access for these groups. Realising the importance of condom programming in ASRHR, SAT strengthened the capacity of CSOs to utilize the UNAIDS global Condom Needs Estimation Tool (CNET) for analysing condom needs in 5 countries focusing on budgeting, procurement, distribution, and accountability for national condom programmes.
